name: Hindu nationalism
summary: Hindu nationalism holds that India is the homeland and holy land of the Hindu nation, whose national life is the Hindu life and to which minorities should adhere. It calls for a unitary state, restriction of conversion, a uniform civil code, cow protection and the recovery of lost territory. Its thinkers reject both capitalism and communism for an integral, culture-first path, and accept armed defence.
scope: The national question as stated by the Hindutva movement's own texts: Savarkar's Hindutva (1923) and Hindu Rashtra Darshan, Golwalkar's We (1939) and Bunch of Thoughts, Upadhyaya's Integral Humanism lectures (chapters 1-3), and the Jana Sangh 1967 and BJP 2019 programmes for the national-unity and cultural items only. Their economic, welfare and general foreign policy programme is left out as the party's, except where the thinkers state it as the nation's cause.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Upadhyaya argues independence means little unless it expresses the nation's own culture (its Chiti), and Golwalkar makes the national ethos the basis of integration.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Upadhyaya absorbs Western science but not Western life, and Golwalkar urges a creative policy assimilating Westernism's science and technology in just proportion with India's own best features.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Savarkar defines a Hindu as one who holds the land from the Indus to the seas as both fatherland and holy land; Golwalkar calls it Bharat Mata.

sacred-nation.rationale: Upadhyaya treats the nation as a living organism with a soul (Chiti) that outlasts its individuals, and Golwalkar speaks of the motherland as sacred.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The RSS resolution Golwalkar records says the thread of inherent national unity has never snapped, and Upadhyaya says the current of national life was not interrupted.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Golwalkar's We and Bunch of Thoughts, and Savarkar's Hindutva (every inch of the soil a sacrificial ground) and Hindu Rashtra Darshan (thousands of martyrs) all honour those who died for the Hindu nation; sainthood is not stated.

patriotic-education.rationale: Only one strand (Golwalkar's RSS texts) states this, and no other strand is shown to share or oppose it, so no position is recorded.

religious-nation.rationale: Savarkar says Hindutva is not a religion but fatherland plus holy land, race and culture, while Golwalkar says national life in Bharat is the Hindu life; the texts point both ways.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Savarkar makes common blood one bond of the Hindu nation and Golwalkar calls the national race the body of the nation, though both describe a mixed Hindu race.

minority-language-support.rationale: Savarkar offered special protection for Muslim language, culture and religion, while Golwalkar's resolution labels linguistic-minority claims communalism; the texts split.

decide-locally.rationale: Golwalkar's resolution wants a unitary state, while Upadhyaya also wants a unitary constitution but with power decentralised down to the lowest unit (the janapada); the strands differ on how local decisions should be.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: A unitary state with provinces subordinate to the Union is the stated aim: Golwalkar's resolution and the 1967 Jana Sangh programme.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Golwalkar's resolution brands linguistic and provincial separatism communalism and demands a unitary state; the Jana Sangh promised to delete Article 370.

right-to-secede.rationale: Golwalkar's resolution wants the desire to secede ended, and Savarkar's Hindu Mahasabha address says Hindusthan must ever remain one and indivisible.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The Jana Sangh promised to delete Article 370 so Kashmir has the same laws as other provinces, and the 2019 programme reiterates abrogation as a position held since the Jana Sangh.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Golwalkar calls land lost to Pakistani and Chinese aggression ours, and the 1967 Jana Sangh programme refuses talks with China or Pakistan unless they vacate the aggression (legible in poor OCR).

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Golwalkar welcomes reunification and Bharat Mata undivided, Savarkar ran the Akhand Hindusthan campaign against the vivisection of India, and Upadhyaya held that the ending of the division must be nurtured in people's minds step by step.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Golwalkar says treating lost land as the aggressor's shows lost will, and the Jana Sangh programme rejects the Tashkent declaration and talks without vacation of aggression.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Savarkar grounds Hindu nationhood in the land as fatherland and holy land, and Golwalkar claims the present Pakistan as immemorially part of the motherland.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Savarkar and the later Golwalkar state equality of citizens before the law, but Golwalkar's 1939 We would leave non-Hindus without even citizen's rights.

separate-church-state.rationale: Only one strand (Golwalkar's RSS texts) states this, and no other strand is shown to share or oppose it, so no position is recorded.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Golwalkar's resolution says conversion subverts loyalty to the nation, is dangerous to its security, and must be stopped; the Jana Sangh promised restrictions on foreign missionaries.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Golwalkar approves the campaign for a ban and the Jana Sangh promised a legal ban; Upadhyaya complained that government would not prohibit it, while Savarkar called cow protection a national duty but rejected cow worship.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The Jana Sangh promised a common civil code so all are equal before law, and Golwalkar's resolution says citizens are equal in secular life with no exclusive rights; neither Savarkar nor Golwalkar names a civil code.

communal-electorates.rationale: Savarkar demands one man one vote irrespective of religion, and the Jana Sangh promised to end separate electorates.

racial-franchise.rationale: Savarkar demands one man one vote irrespective of race or religion and later Golwalkar says citizens are equal in secular life, but Golwalkar's 1939 We would leave non-Hindus without even citizen's rights.

political-violence-never.rationale: Savarkar calls absolute non-violence impractical and Golwalkar's chapter on non-violence or imbecility says strength is the basis of survival.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Savarkar approves armed defence against aggression and Golwalkar attacks perverse notions of non-violence in the face of attack.

revolution-justified.rationale: Savarkar praises armed revolution, but Golwalkar's remark is about the Marxist slogan of revolution and no other strand states a general position, so no position is recorded.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Golwalkar ridicules officers urged to world-mindedness, and Savarkar urges Hindus to join the army and militarise.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Golwalkar holds the strong devour the weak, Savarkar urges militarisation, and the Jana Sangh programme builds up the armed forces.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Golwalkar derides non-alignment as a football's neutrality, while the 1967 Jana Sangh programme promises an independent foreign policy with ties to countries irrespective of their bloc allegiance; the strands split.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Only one strand (Golwalkar's RSS texts) states this, and no other strand is shown to share or oppose it, so no position is recorded.

defeat-communism.rationale: Golwalkar's chapter on Communists treats them as an internal threat and the Jana Sangh promised to put down those working for China under treason law.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Golwalkar's chapter on the challenge of the times and Upadhyaya's Integral Humanism reject both capitalism and communism as materialist and offer an integral Bharatiya alternative.

class-collaboration.rationale: Savarkar says the claims of capital and labour are to be coordinated and Upadhyaya makes cooperation, not conflict, the law of culture.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Upadhyaya rejects Marx's analysis and Golwalkar rejects the class-war-ridden Marxist structure and says revolution slogans invite armed strife.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Upadhyaya and Golwalkar reject materialism and place the nation's Chiti and dharma, not production, as the driver of national life.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Upadhyaya says man is body, mind, intellect and soul, and Golwalkar says the Hindu solution is not based on materialism but on the primacy of the spirit.

universal-morality.rationale: Upadhyaya says ethical principles are discovered, not framed, and Golwalkar calls dharma the eternal law of life and the nation a vehicle of universal truths.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Upadhyaya presents Bharatiya culture as integrated and able to point the way where Western thought is confused, and Golwalkar calls Hindu thought uniquely tolerant.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Upadhyaya says foreign isms cannot be adopted wholesale, and Golwalkar says Marxist and Western ideas are unsuited to national renovation and that the Constitution lacks Indian political precepts.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Upadhyaya calls conflict regression and cooperation the law of culture, while Savarkar calls survival of the fittest the rule among nations and Golwalkar calls the law of the jungle the basic rule of relations between nations; the strands split.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Only one strand (Golwalkar's RSS texts) states this, and no other strand is shown to share or oppose it, so no position is recorded.

total-state.rationale: Golwalkar warns that a state dominating all human activity leaves the individual a slave, and scholarship says Integral Humanism rejects statism for individual liberty within social responsibility.

public-ownership.rationale: Only one strand (Golwalkar's RSS texts) states this, and no other strand is shown to share or oppose it, so no position is recorded.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Upadhyaya notes it eliminated individual freedom and Golwalkar says the dictatorship of the proletariat became the dictatorship of the party's dictator.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Golwalkar heads his discussion with the evil of capitalism and Upadhyaya says capitalism let the industrial worker be exploited.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Upadhyaya says the past cannot be disowned, and Golwalkar says all should consider the Hindu heritage and history as their own.

restore-past-order.rationale: Upadhyaya rejects restarting from where the nation stood a thousand years ago, and Savarkar calls social customs like untouchability suicidal and urges industrialisation.

religion-illusion.rationale: Golwalkar and Upadhyaya reject materialism and make dharma the basis of national life.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Only one strand (Golwalkar's RSS texts) states this, and no other strand is shown to share or oppose it, so no position is recorded.

notes: Golwalkar's 1939 We would leave non-Hindus without citizen's rights, which the RSS no longer endorses; his later Bunch of Thoughts and Savarkar state equality of citizens, so equal-rights answers are low. Not reached: Upadhyaya's Integral Humanism chapter 4 (state, economy) and Savarkar's cow, caste and language essays, so those themes are null. The 1967 Jana Sangh OCR is poor; only legible items were used. Themes searched: nation, territory, minorities, language, religion and state, means, world, economy and culture. Strand pass (2026-10-30): answers resting on one strand were rechecked against the other strands' texts; seven (Golwalkar-only: patriotic-education, separate-church-state, empower-international-orgs, state-class-instrument, total-state, public-ownership, uniformed-youth) are null, four are splits (stay-neutral-between-blocs, competition-drives-progress, racial-franchise, revolution-justified), and the rest gained a second strand's source. Economy and philosophy answers are kept only where Golwalkar's and Upadhyaya's texts present them as part of the national cause. Deepen pass (2026-10-30): added Savarkar's Historic Statements and Samagra vol. 7, secondary RSS-press volumes on Upadhyaya (Parts III and VI, Concept of the Rashtra) and a 2025 RSS resolution. decide-locally became a split, revive-national-language and revolution-justified are null, the uniform civil code was lowered to +1, and six answers were added. Integral Humanism chapter 4 and the Jana Sangh Party Documents volumes were not found openly. Review (2026-10-30): military-superiority nulled (a single strand; Upadhyaya's passage does not state superiority); independent-nuclear-deterrent and self-reliance-over-aid lowered to medium, since their second strand rests on the reference volumes on Upadhyaya.
